changes.reason: Lowering the frozen edge to 2.5 eV worsened the truncated eta_2 (25.1 to 34.3 meV). Raising it past the original 3.92 eV pins more of the entangled conduction-band bottom, which is where the truncated error sits. Capacity allows up to 14.55 eV.

diagnosis: Diamond, with the 8 C 2s+2p PAOs. The untruncated model is accurate (17.45 meV), all other checks pass, and the spreads are tight and even (ratio 1.11). The truncated eta_2 failure comes entirely from the bottom of the conduction band. Below E_F+1 eV the truncated model stays within about 9–12 meV. In the E_F+2 eV window, band 5 (CBM at +1.35 eV on the path, off the 16^3 mesh near 0.4–0.5 along the Γ–X/K direction) is off by up to 305 meV once hoppings beyond 10.09 Å are cut. Those weak long-range tails come from how the entangled conduction states between the frozen edge and the free region are disentangled; they do not come from the projectors. The run's own history shows which way to move: lowering dis_froz_max from the paper's 3.92 eV to 2.5 eV made the truncated eta_2 worse (25.06 to 34.26 meV). So pinning more of the low conduction manifold is what keeps the CB-bottom subspace smooth and short-ranged. I'm reversing that change and going further: dis_froz_max = 5.0 eV. frozen_capacity allows up to 14.55 eV (7 states at most against 8 functions), and validate_deck accepts the deck. I'm keeping dis_proj_max = 0.99, which gave the earlier improvement (30.90 to 25.06).

truncated_hopping_eta2.note: eta_2 = 15.17 meV with hoppings longer than r_c = L_BvK/4 = 10.09 Ang (|R + tau_j - tau_i|) removed (447 of 4905 lattice vectors keep a hopping; untruncated 1.83 meV)
truncated_hopping_eta2.l_bvk_definition: shortest non-zero vector of the mp_grid superlattice
truncated_hopping_eta2.truncation_length: hopping length |R + tau_j - tau_i|, tau = the Wannier centres
